prerequisites: Owned seeded lab aoauth (openlaw-docs-9d2b1705-aoauth) built from 4ca41822, with a local OIDC fixture (oauth2-mock-server 9.2.0) serving two issuers on the lab network. Daniel Okafor (Administrator), Nadia Haddad (Legal Team Member), seeded and Portal-created Business Users, and disposable doc032-auth-* accounts, each in its own browser context.
Owned unseeded lab aowiz (openlaw-docs-9d2b1705-aowiz) with the fictional first Administrator DOC-032 admin-org Avery Morgan for the wizard email step and the Settings email pane.
scenarios.expected: Administrators and Legal Team Members sign in with the methods enabled under Legal User Authentication. An Administrator with a password keeps emergency password sign-in when Email and password is off. Business Users sign in only with the methods enabled under Business Portal Authentication. Invalid issuer/relay, denied domain have recoverable outcomes without exposing secrets.
scenarios.actual: 48 recorded administrator steps passed. Two policy cards with Email and password, Email magic link, Single sign-on (SSO) and Require two-factor authentication; each change showed Saved; a card with no method gave "Enable at least one sign-in method."; the SSO switch was unavailable with "Configure an identity provider below to enable single sign-on.". With Legal Email and password off, Daniel still signed in with a password and Nadia was refused; with only SSO on, the page offered Administrator sign-in and Daniel signed in. Pending invitations, including one off the allowed domains, got 5-minute single-use links that activated them; a reused and an expired link gave no session; a Business User on the staff page landed in the Portal. Adding and removing northwind.example: an unapproved address got no link and no account; removing one of two domains refused new accounts but kept existing Business Users (new link, held session, earlier link, password). Removing the last domain showed "No domains allowed yet. New users must be invited individually.", stored every Business method off, made all four switches unavailable with "Add an allowed email domain to enable Business User sign-in options." (SSO: "Add an allowed email domain and configure an identity provider to enable single sign-on."), kept Require two-factor authentication at its value, left Invite user with staff roles only, showed "Sign-in is unavailable. Contact your administrator." on the Portal page, refused the existing Business User, and kept a held session; adding a domain left the methods off until turned on. Turning off Business Email magic link stopped an earlier link. Add provider opened Display name, Provider ID, Issuer URL, Email domains, Client ID, Client secret with "Separate several domains with commas..."; an unreachable issuer was refused and nothing stored; registration showed the callback http://127.0.0.1:43351/api/auth/sso/callback, listed the name, domain and Configured, and changed no policy; the secret was never returned. With one provider the staff page offered a single Continue with single sign-on button and an invited account signed in (row Active); an uninvited helix.example identity got no staff role. Edit {name} had no Provider ID; a blank secret kept it and a replacement rotated it, both followed by working sign-ins; an unreachable issuer on edit kept the old configuration. A second provider with harbor.example, ops.northwind.example used the same callback; exact, subdomain and parent domains were refused naming the holder ("... assigned to the identity provider DOC-032 Harbor IdP ..."). With two providers the page asked for Email and routed helix.example to http://oidc:8080 and harbor.example to http://oidc:8082; unlisted.example showed "No single sign-on provider is set up for unlisted.example. Check the address or contact your administrator." with the other methods still offered. A provider whose stored configuration was blanked showed Missing credentials and returned to Configured after Edit. Business Portal SSO signed in an existing Business User, still after its domain was removed, while a new identity was refused. Remove {name} had no confirmation and accounts kept their rows (a sign-in link still worked); removing the last provider turned SSO off in both cards; with SSO as the only Legal method it left the staff page on "Sign-in is unavailable. Contact your administrator." with no Administrator sign-in, and the open Administrator session turned Email and password back on. Require two-factor authentication sent an Administrator without an authenticator to enrollment, required a code on each new session, and applied to magic links, SSO and emergency password sign-in. The actual role decided the methods on either sign-in page. On aowiz, the wizard email step (Port 587/465/25, refused smtp:// and host:port, STARTTLS failure, Replace relay, Keep current relay, unreachable relay, Clear relay) and the Settings pane (Replace relay, Cancel, no Clear relay, change applied without restart) behaved as the guide states; the test email read "OpenLaw test email", "Outbound email works", Sent through and From.

prerequisites: The operator responsibility, exercised as compose overlays on the owned labs (phase.sh): SMTP_URL/SMTP_FROM unset, SMTP_URL without SMTP_FROM, both set, BASE_URL removed, and the OIDC fixture container. Each change was checked in the browser as the lab Administrator.
scenarios.expected: Test mail reaches the controlled sink through the active configuration source; environment precedence and locked environment settings behave as the guide states; the identity-provider client and the instance address follow the deployment.
scenarios.actual: 10 recorded operator steps passed. With SMTP_URL set and SMTP_FROM empty, the wizard step and Settings, Advanced, Outbound email showed "The deployment environment sets SMTP_URL but not SMTP_FROM, so mail cannot be sent. Set SMTP_FROM in the environment."; Send test email was unavailable and an invitation was refused although a complete relay was saved in the app. With both set, the wizard step read "Outbound email is set by the deployment environment. Mail is sent from DOC-032 Environment <env-relay@helix.example>." with no relay form, a direct save answered 409, Settings showed "Managed by your deployment configuration. Contact your system administrator to change the relay." with only Send test email, and the test mail and an invitation came from env-relay@helix.example, not the stored relay. Removing the override and recreating app and worker returned Settings to the stored relay (Sender "DOC-032 Stored" <stored-relay@helix.example>) and its test mail. The OIDC client came from the fixture issuer; the callback used the instance address. With BASE_URL set, Instance address read "Application address Deployment configuration · Read only" and the callback used it; with BASE_URL removed the field was editable (Default, http://localhost:3000), a saved address waited for a restart ("Settings saved. Restart the API and worker to apply changes."), and after the restart sign-ins and the callback used the saved address.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the source reviewer; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

The identity providers were a local OIDC fixture with two issuers (oauth2-mock-server 9.2.0), not live vendors; V-C37 requires a browser walkthrough, not a live-provider check. This version has no SAML setup, as the guide states.
'Missing credentials' was produced by fault injection on the owned lab (the provider's stored oidc_config set to '{}').

operator is a responsibility, not an OpenLaw account. Operator steps were compose overlay changes on the owned labs aoauth and aowiz, checked in the browser as the lab Administrator. The labs were destroyed after the walk.
With BASE_URL removed, the API accepts requests only from its default origin, so the Administrator reached the lab as http://localhost:3000 through a browser host mapping to the lab port.

The registry's 'An Administrator with a password keeps emergency password sign-in when Email and password is off' holds while Legal User Authentication keeps another method. After the last identity provider is removed from an SSO-only Legal policy the staff page offers no password form (walkthrough.json productBugs); the guide states this.

Product bug reproduced (walkthrough.json productBugs): on a fresh install that never saved an allowed domain, Settings shows the Business methods off while the stored policy still lets a Business User sign in with a password. The guide's empty-list paragraph describes the Settings display and the state after removing the last domain, which the walk confirmed.

An unreachable issuer is refused with the generic 'The server could not be reached. Try again.' and invalid relay hosts with 'One or more request fields are invalid.'. Both are recoverable; the guide gives the corrective action without quoting them.
